## Known-good invariants [#known-good-invariants]

```text
adb reverse --list               → host-16 tcp:18080 tcp:18080
settings get global http_proxy   → 127.0.0.1:18080
/data/adb/fsrv/ctl status        → running pid=<n> listen=127.0.0.1:27042
zygiskd status                   → modules64: 3,zygisk_vector,hma_oss_zygisk,playintegrityfix
magisk --denylist ls             → empty
```

If any of those drift, run `pentestctl fix` and read [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting).

# Root hiding (/docs/stealth)

Root is required for everything else here, so hiding it is a permanent tax. This rig hides the *mechanisms* (su binary, Magisk daemon, Zygisk libs, Frida) rather than trying to make a detector believe the device is unmodified — the attestation layer handles the "is this a real phone" question separately.

## What is hidden, and how [#what-is-hidden-and-how]

| Mechanism | Visibility | Mitigation in this rig |
|---|---|---|
| `su` binary / `magisk` | filesystem paths | Magisk's own mount/masking; app denylist empty so modules keep working |
| Zygisk injection | `/proc/<pid>/maps`, dlopen paths | Zygisk Next `memory-type anonymous` → no file-backed libs |
| Module mounts | `/proc/<pid>/mountinfo` | only whitelisted apps see them (default policy) |
| Frida | process name, listening port, string `frida-server` | renamed `hluda`, loopback only, no default port on LAN |
| Package enumeration | `getPackageInfo` / `queryIntentActivities` | HMA-OSS, scoped per target with `hma` |
| Attestation | keystore chain | TrickyStore + keybox (see [Attestation](/docs/attestation)) |

## Zygisk Next knobs [#zygisk-next-knobs]

`/data/adb/modules/zygisksu/bin/zygiskd` is the control surface:

```bash
zygiskd status
zygiskd enforce-denylist enabled      # honour Magisk's denylist
zygiskd denylist-policy default       # default | whitelist
zygiskd memory-type anonymous         # default | anonymous
zygiskd disable-zygisk false
```

Current config (survives reboot):

```text
inject_state:1  denylist_policy:0 (default)  enforce_denylist:1  memory_type:1 (anonymous)
modules64: 3,zygisk_vector,hma_oss_zygisk,playintegrityfix
```

### The whitelist trap [#the-whitelist-trap]

`denylist-policy whitelist` means *only* listed packages get module injection — attractive for stealth, and it **breaks WebView apps**:

```text
WebView renderer (…:sandboxed_process0, isolated uid u0ai9000) does not match the package name
→ no modules injected → no CA / no unpinning in the sandboxed renderer
→ net_error -202 (SSL handshake failed) on every page
```

Verified and reverted. Keep `default`, and keep the app you are testing **out** of Magisk's denylist.

## Magisk denylist: keep it empty [#magisk-denylist-keep-it-empty]

```bash
adb shell su -c 'magisk --denylist ls'      # expected: empty
```

If an app is in the denylist, Magisk strips module mounts from it — which is exactly where TrickyStore and PIF need to be. Hiding by denylisting is incompatible with spoofing. Choose one per app.

## Traps [#traps]

<Callout type="error" title="`magisk --denylist rm <pkg> <process>` segfaults the daemon">
Two-argument form kills `magiskd`; afterwards `magisk -v` says
`Cannot connect to daemon: Connection refused (os error 111)` and `su` is gone with it. Only a reboot recovers. Always pass a single package argument.
</Callout>

<Callout type="info" title="Magisk 31.1 removed 'Hide the Magisk app'">
There is no stub-repackaging option in Settings and no CLI equivalent. Package-level hiding is HMA-OSS's job; keep that expectation straight when a detector lists installed packages.
</Callout>

## HMA-OSS: hiding packages from one app at a time [#hma-oss-hiding-packages-from-one-app-at-a-time]

HMA-OSS (`hma_oss_zygisk`, manager `org.frknkrc44.hma_oss`) hooks package queries inside a chosen app and filters the answer. It is **scoped per target**: you say "when *this* app asks, act as if these packages do not exist".

### The file that matters [#the-file-that-matters]

```text
/data/misc/hide_my_applist_bkpzksjqktswmspy/config.json
```

One JSON document, schema `configVersion: 95`, with a `scope` object keyed by target package. Each entry is an `AppConfig`:

```json
"com.example.target": {
  "useWhitelist": false,
  "excludeSystemApps": true,
  "applyPresets": ["detector_apps","root_apps","shizuku_dhizuku","sus_apps","xposed"],
  "applySettingsPresets": ["accessibility","dev_options"],
  "extraSettings": {"settingsList": []},
  "extraAppList": [], "extraOppositeAppList": []
}
```

Preset names (they are the module's, not yours): apps = `accessibility_apps, custom_rom, detector_apps, root_apps, shizuku_dhizuku, sus_apps, xposed`; settings = `accessibility, dev_options, input_method`. The five app presets above are what you want against a root-detector: Magisk, KeyAttestation, Frida tooling, other test apps, Xposed-era leftovers.

### Doing it from the host, not the UI [#doing-it-from-the-host-not-the-ui]

```bash
hma show                          # current scope entries
hma hide com.example.target       # 5 app presets + 2 settings presets (defaults)
hma hide com.example.target --presets root_apps,sus_apps --settings dev_options
hma targets                       # what the scope currently names
hma unhide com.example.target     # needs a reboot, see the trap below
hma backup / hma restore          # snapshot the config before experiments
```

`hma` writes the config in place over `su`, so HMA's `FileObserver(configFile, CLOSE_WRITE or ATTRIB)` picks it up. Logcat then shows `(HMA-Service) Config loaded` (three times per write — `chmod` fires `ATTRIB` as well).

<Callout type="error" title="Un-hiding does not take effect until you reboot">
`HMAServiceDataHolder.shouldHideFromUid()` answers from a `uidHideCache` *before* it looks at the config, and only the manager-app pipe clears that cache — the file-reload path does not. Measured: `hma hide` on a live app works immediately (257 → 252 packages, Magisk hidden), `hma unhide` changes the file and nothing else. Reboot to un-hide.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warn" title="The manager app only saves on `onPause`">
If you configure HMA in its UI and press Back, nothing is written — `AppSettingsV2Fragment` persists in `onPause`. Press HOME (or leave the app) to commit. This is why hand-editing `config.json` with `hma` is the less surprising path.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warn" title="A config.json created *after* boot is never watched">
The `FileObserver` is constructed at boot even when the file is missing. If HMA has never written a config on this boot, your first `hma hide` needs one reboot before it has any effect. Check with `hma show` — if it is empty and you just created a scope, reboot, then re-apply.
</Callout>

## Verifying hiding actually works [#verifying-hiding-actually-works]

**Measure with an app that declares `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`.** Without it, Android 11+ package-visibility filtering makes every app look clean:

```text
pm list packages                     → 255 packages
Target getInstalledPackages(0)       → 91     (no QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES)
pinning-demo getInstalledPackages(0) → 90     (no QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES)
ApplistDetector (QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES) → 252/256 and Magisk visible or not
```

Use `apks/ApplistDetector.V2.4.apk` (`icu.nullptr.applistdetector`, Dr-TSNG) as the detector:

```bash
asu 'am start -n icu.nullptr.applistdetector/.MainActivity'
# then read its "Installed apps" count and the Magisk/KeyAttestation rows
```

Measured on this rig, detector scoped, before vs after reboot:

| state | installed count | `com.topjohnwu.magisk` |
|---|---|---|
| baseline, no scope | 256 | visible |
| scoped + reboot | 252 | hidden |
| live-added scope (Chrome) | 257 → 252 | visible → hidden, no reboot needed |

HMA never hides a target app from itself, so the detector still lists `icu.nullptr.applistdetector` — that is correct behaviour, not a leak.

Hiding does not disturb spoofing: after HMA was enabled, KeyAttestation still reported the keybox chain (`CN=Droid CA2, O=Google LLC`) and `Bootloader is locked`.

```bash
# module mounts visible to a normal app vs a module-injected app
adb shell su -c 'wc -l < /proc/<settings-pid>/mountinfo'     # ~157
adb shell su -c 'wc -l < /proc/<target-pid>/mountinfo'       # ~167 (10 module mounts)

# no zygisk/tricky libs mapped
adb shell su -c 'grep -cE "zygisk|tricky" /proc/<target-pid>/maps'   # 0
```

The 10-mount difference is the honest answer to "is injection scoped": non-target apps see zero module mounts.

## What this does not hide [#what-this-does-not-hide]

- **Emulator fingerprints** (`ro.kernel.qemu`, `goldfish` hardware, sensor set). Apps that check them are dealt with by `intercept`'s root/emulator detection bypass, not by this layer.
- **A keybox that is revoked** — that is server-side truth, see [Attestation](/docs/attestation).
- **Your traffic** — it leaves from the host's IP through mitmproxy.

# Command reference (/docs/tooling)

Everything is in `~/mobsec/bin` (already on `PATH`). All commands assume the emulator is running.

## Health & control [#health--control]

### `pentestctl` [#pentestctl]
```bash
pentestctl status     # device, root, zygisk, attestation (keybox expiry!), frida, interception
pentestctl fix        # nettap on + restart frida-server; repairs reboot damage
```
Sections and what they read:

| Section | Source of truth |
|---|---|
| device | `adb shell getprop` |
| root | `su -c id`, `su -c magisk -v` |
| zygisk | `zygiskd status` |
| attestation | `/data/adb/tricky_store/{keybox.xml,target.txt}` + `kbcheck.py` |
| frida | `/data/adb/fsrv/ctl status` |
| interception | `/tmp/mitm.pid`, `adb reverse --list`, `settings get global http_proxy`, flow count, cert-fixer log |

### `nettap` [#nettap]
```bash
nettap on [port]      # mitmdump (idempotent) + adb reverse + global proxy
nettap off            # kill mitmdump, remove proxy/reverse
nettap status         # proxy, reverse, pid, addon path, flow count
```
Env: `ADDON` (dump.py), `FLOWDIR`, `INTEREST`, `PORT`. `nettap on` refuses to start if the addon or `mitmdump` is missing instead of dying silently.

### `snap` [#snap]
```bash
snap list             # snapshots + size + newest file mtime
snap save [name]      # default 'logged-in'
snap load [name]      # boots with -snapshot -no-snapshot-save (~25 s)
snap rm [name]
snap boot             # cold boot the AVD
```

## Frida [#frida]

### `fspawn <pkg> [profile] [frida args…]` [#fspawn-pkg-profile-frida-args]
Profiles: `trace` (default), `web`, `attest`, `spy`, `intercept`, `full`, `raw`. See [Frida](/docs/frida#profiles).
```bash
fspawn com.example.app intercept
fspawn com.example.app raw -l ~/hooks.js
```

### `fdp [pkg] [port]` [#fdp-pkg-port]
Finds `webview_devtools_remote_<pid>` in `/proc/net/unix` (auto-detects the foreground app when `pkg` is omitted), forwards `:9222`, prints the target list.

### `cdp url|eval "<js>"|watch [secs]` [#cdp-urleval-jswatch-secs]
Minimal CDP client (python3 + `websockets`). `eval` awaits promises; `watch` streams console/network events.

### `session` [#session]
```bash
session            # harvest -> ~/.mobsec/session/<ts>.json + latest.json
session show       # pretty-print
session cookie     # just the Cookie header value
```
Merges `document.cookie`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` from the WebView with the newest flow's cookie header (httpOnly cookies are invisible to JS). `TARGET=target session` restricts the page match.

### `medusa-export` [#medusa-export]
```bash
medusa-export list [filter]
medusa-export export NAME... | --set core|web|dump
medusa-export path NAME
```

## Traffic [#traffic]

### `replay` [#replay]
```bash
replay --grep 'chat/loadInitialData' --session
replay --grep X --patch 'a.b=42' --patch 'items[0].id=1' --dry
replay --grep X --method POST --path /other --body '{"q":"x"}'
replay --grep X --header 'x-test: 1' --remove-header cookie -x --full --save out.json
```
Defaults to exactly what the app sent (same headers, cookie, body). `-x` sends through mitmproxy (captured as evidence). `--save` writes the response body.

### `recon` [#recon]
```bash
recon <apk|package> [--deep] [-o DIR]
```
Writes `~/.mobsec/recon/<pkg>-<ts>/report.md` + `raw/`. See [Static recon](/docs/recon).

### `entry` [#entry]
Turns the manifest into copy-paste attack commands — one `adb shell am start|broadcast|content` line per exported component and deep link.
```bash
entry com.example.app                 # attack sheet
entry com.example.app --run            # and fire every probe
entry com.example.app --only links -o /tmp/sheet.txt
```
The sheet lists exported activities/services/receivers with their required permissions, content providers (including `exported=false` + `grantUriPermissions=true`), every `scheme://host` deep link, and `pm get-app-links` state.

### `pull-data` [#pull-data]
The honest replacement for `adb backup` (blocked on API 31+): root-tars the app's private dir, pulls it, and summarises.
```bash
pull-data com.example.app                 # -> ~/.mobsec/data/<pkg>/
pull-data com.example.app --sql           # + row counts for every sqlite db
pull-data com.example.app --grep token    # grep the pull
pull-data com.example.app --no-pull       # re-summarise only
```
Reports the biggest files, every SQLite database with tables/row counts, `shared_prefs` and JSON lines that look like secrets, and pulls `/sdcard/Android/data/<pkg>` too. Writes `summary.txt` next to the extracted tree.

## Attestation, integrity and hiding [#attestation-integrity-and-hiding]

### `setup-keybox.sh` / `keybox-refresh` [#setup-keyboxsh--keybox-refresh]
```bash
setup-keybox.sh --check                 # validate the installed keybox only
setup-keybox.sh --file my-keybox.xml    # install a local one
keybox-refresh [--force] [--min-days 7] [--dry-run]
```
`keybox-refresh` refreshes automatically only when the leaf is close to expiry or revoked, validates candidates with `kbcheck.py --strict`, and backs up the old keybox. It is wired to a systemd user timer. See [Attestation](/docs/attestation).

### `hma` [#hma]
Root-hiding scope editor for HMA-OSS (writes `config.json` over `su`, reloads live).
```bash
hma show
hma hide com.example.app [--presets root_apps,sus_apps] [--settings dev_options]
hma unhide com.example.app               # takes effect after a reboot
hma backup / hma restore
hma targets / hma presets
```
Un-hiding needs a reboot (uid cache); a `config.json` created *after* boot needs one reboot before it is watched. See [Root hiding](/docs/stealth).

### `integrity` [#integrity]
Play Integrity verdict from SPIC, scraped out of logcat.
```bash
integrity     # human-readable verdict
integrity --json     # raw JSON
```
Expect `UNEVALUATED` on this AVD — it is Google declining to grade an emulator with no account, not a rig failure. See [Play Integrity](/docs/integrity).

## Device helpers [#device-helpers]

### `asu` [#asu]
Runs a root shell snippet without the `adb shell su -c "…"` quoting nightmare:
```bash
asu 'for p in /data/adb/modules/*; do echo $p; done'
```

### `uitap` [#uitap]
Text-driven UI automation (`uiautomator dump` under the hood) — survives layout changes that break fixed coordinates:
```bash
uitap dump
uitap click "Login"
uitap click "^Allow$" --exact
uitap wait "Logged in" --timeout 20
```

### `apktool` [#apktool]
Wrapper around the pinned `apktool_3.0.3.jar` (`apktool d app.apk -o out`).

### `docs` [#docs]
The documentation site you are reading, served locally.
```bash
docs serve            # mkdocs serve on 127.0.0.1:8000 (background, pid in /tmp/mkdocs.pid)
docs serve --lan      # bind 0.0.0.0 so other machines can read it (needs a firewall rule, see below)
docs build            # mkdocs build --strict
docs status           # running? bound where? which URLs answer? firewall reminder
docs open | docs stop
```

For permanent LAN sharing there is a user unit, `mobsec-docs.service`
(`systemctl --user enable --now mobsec-docs`), and `sudo ufw allow 8000/tcp` once — `ufw`'s default
inbound policy is `DROP`, so a bound port is not a reachable port.

## Host environment [#host-environment]

```bash
java -version          # 21 (jadx/apktool/apkanalyzer)
frida --version        # 17.27.5
mitmdump --version     # 12.3.1
apkid / apkleaks / mobsfscan / objection / scrcpy / adb / emulator
python3 --version      # 3.12
```

## Cheat sheet [#cheat-sheet]

```bash
# the whole loop, one line each
snap load logged-in && pentestctl fix
nettap on
recon com.example.app --deep
fspawn com.example.app intercept
fdp && cdp url
session && replay --grep 'api/' --session --dry
```

# Troubleshooting (/docs/troubleshooting)

Ordered by how often each one actually happens.

## The five-minute triage [#the-five-minute-triage]

```bash
pentestctl status            # which section is red?
pentestctl fix               # repairs reverse + frida
adb devices                  # is the emulator even up?
curl -s -x 127.0.0.1:18080 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://example.org
tail -20 /tmp/mitm.log
```

If `pentestctl status` is green but the app is silent, the problem is almost always **inside the app** (dead proxy in a cached connection, app not restarted, wrong package).

## Symptom → cause [#symptom--cause]

| Symptom | Most likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| App spins forever, zero flows | `adb reverse` died on reboot | `nettap on` |
| Zero flows but `nettap status` says up | app cached a dead connection | force-stop + relaunch; `fspawn … intercept` |
| GMS/Play Store TLS errors in `/tmp/mitm.log` | Cert-Fixer didn't run this boot | reboot, then `pentestctl status \| grep Cert-Fixer` |
| `frida-ps` hangs or "unable to connect" | frida-server died | `adb shell su -c '/data/adb/fsrv/ctl start'` |
| `Failed to spawn` but package installed | wrong package name / user profile | `adb shell pm list packages \| grep -i name` |
| App crashes at startup under Frida | a script broke it | `fspawn <pkg> raw`, add scripts one at a time |
| `net_error -202` on every WebView page | whitelist denylist policy | `zygiskd denylist-policy default` (see below) |
| Attestation rejected (`4202`) after a keybox change | `target.txt` missing the package, or keybox revoked/expired | `pentestctl status \| grep keybox`, add package, force-stop app |
| `magisk -v` → `Cannot connect to daemon` | daemon segfaulted by a two-arg `--denylist rm` | reboot |
| Emulator won't boot after a bad snapshot | snapshot captured a broken mount | `snap boot` (cold), verify, `snap save <newname>` |
| A command you rely on suddenly behaves differently | a `~/mobsec/bin` helper shadows it (PATH order) | `pentestctl status` → *host commands*; rename the helper |

## Trap list (all hit for real here) [#trap-list-all-hit-for-real-here]

### 1. `adb reverse` does not survive a reboot [#1-adb-reverse-does-not-survive-a-reboot]
`settings put global http_proxy` **does**. Result: the app points at `127.0.0.1:18080` where nothing listens, and every request hangs with no error. `pentestctl fix` handles it.

### 2. `frida … < /dev/null` exits instantly [#2-frida---devnull-exits-instantly]
No tty → REPL dies. Use a fifo:
```bash
mkfifo /tmp/f; sleep 900 > /tmp/f &
fspawn <pkg> intercept < /tmp/f > /tmp/frida.log 2>&1 &
```

### 3. `pkill -f` kills your own shell [#3-pkill--f-kills-your-own-shell]
`pkill -f qemu-system` or `pkill -f 'frida -U -f pkg'` matches the `bash -c "<that command>"` wrapper and kills the invoking shell (exit 143). Record the PID and `kill <pid>`.

### 4. `magisk --denylist rm <pkg> <process>` segfaults magiskd [#4-magisk---denylist-rm-pkg-process-segfaults-magiskd]
Always one argument: `magisk --denylist rm <pkg>`. Recovery from the crash requires a reboot.

### 5. Whitelist denylist policy breaks WebView renderers [#5-whitelist-denylist-policy-breaks-webview-renderers]
`zygiskd denylist-policy whitelist` avoids injecting into non-listed apps, but renderer sandbox processes (`…:sandboxed_process0`, isolated uid) never match the package, so the CA and unpinning hooks are missing inside WebView → `SSL handshake failed; net_error -202`. Keep `default`.

### 6. `adb shell su -c '…'` mangles quotes and loops [#6-adb-shell-su--c--mangles-quotes-and-loops]
Multi-line snippets with `for`/`while` fail with `syntax error: unexpected 'do'`. Use `asu '…'`, which writes a script and runs it.

### 7. Don't grep `/data/adb/modules/zygisksu/` recursively [#7-dont-grep-dataadbmoduleszygisksu-recursively]
Its webroot has megabytes of i18n JSON and floods your terminal (and your context). Read specific files.

### 8. mitmproxy does not hot-reload addons [#8-mitmproxy-does-not-hot-reload-addons]
Edited `mitm/dump.py`? `nettap off && nettap on`, otherwise you keep the old behaviour (this is how a "fixed" filename bug appears unfixed).

### 9. PlayIntegrityFork v19 is arm-only [#9-playintegrityfork-v19-is-arm-only]
On x86_64 it silently never loads (`zygiskd status` stops listing `playintegrityfix`). Use the 4.9 x86_64 build.

### 10. Medusa's `shared_preferences` module kills WebView apps [#10-medusas-shared_preferences-module-kills-webview-apps]
`java.lang.NullPointerException … SharedPreferences$Editor.apply() on a null object reference` inside `WebViewChromiumFactoryProvider`. Not in any default profile.

## Recovery runbook [#recovery-runbook]

```bash
# 1. device
snap boot                     # or: snap load logged-in
adb wait-for-device
pentestctl status

# 2. root/modules
adb shell su -c 'zygiskd status'
adb shell su -c 'cat /data/adb/tricky_store/target.txt'
adb shell su -c 'grep -o "DeviceID=\"[^\"]*\"" /data/adb/tricky_store/keybox.xml'

# 3. frida
adb shell su -c '/data/adb/fsrv/ctl status' || adb shell su -c '/data/adb/fsrv/ctl start'
frida-ps -U | head -3

# 4. interception
nettap on
ls -t /tmp/mtflows/*.txt | head -2

# 5. CA trust for system apps
adb shell su -c 'tail -1 /data/local/tmp/cert-fixer.log'   # want "execution completed"
```

If step 5 is stale, reboot once — Cert-Fixer only mounts at `post-fs-data`.

## Logs worth knowing [#logs-worth-knowing]

| Log | What |
|---|---|
| `/tmp/mitm.log` | mitmdump stdout (`-v`), TLS failures, addon exceptions |
| `/tmp/mtflows/_err.log` | addon write failures |
| `/tmp/frida.log` | your `fspawn` output when run in background |
| `/data/local/tmp/cert-fixer.log` | CA mount result per boot |
| `adb logcat` | app crashes: `adb logcat -v time \| grep -iE 'AndroidRuntime\|FATAL'` |

## When nothing makes sense [#when-nothing-makes-sense]

Compare against a state you know worked:

```bash
snap load logged-in
pentestctl fix
fspawn tech.httptoolkit.pinning_demo intercept    # known-good pinning target
```

If the demo app also fails, the rig is broken. If only your target fails, the target has an additional defence — collect `fspawn … trace` output and read the `rootcheck`/`tls` lines before guessing.

# Daily workflow (/docs/workflow)

The loop that matters: **restore → verify → instrument → capture → replay → document.**

## 1. Restore a known-good state [#1-restore-a-known-good-state]

```bash
snap load logged-in     # AVD snapshot: apps + logged-in session (~25 s)
pentestctl fix          # adb reverse dies on reboot; mitm addon may be down
pentestctl status       # read it, don't assume
```

If you changed anything device-wide (new module, new CA, new keybox), `snap save` a **new** snapshot name instead of overwriting `logged-in` — snapshots carry the mount state, and a stale snapshot can bring back a broken CA mount.

## 2. Start the capture [#2-start-the-capture]

```bash
nettap on               # mitmdump + adb reverse + global proxy
```

`nettap on` is idempotent. For pinned apps you can even drop the global proxy afterwards (`adb shell settings put global http_proxy :0`) — `fspawn … intercept` redirects connections in-process, so capture continues.

## 3. Instrument, don't guess [#3-instrument-dont-guess]

```bash
fspawn com.example.app intercept    # pinning + CA injection + root-detect off
fspawn com.example.app trace        # core + rootcheck + TLS + WebView debug
fspawn com.example.app spy          # stolen Medusa modules (anti-root, okhttp, sqlite)
```

Rules of thumb:

- **WebView/Tauri/Cordova app?** You get 80% of the answer from `fdp` + `cdp eval` — DOM, storage, fetch wrappers, console. Do that before native hooking.
- **Native pinning / keystore work?** `intercept` first, then `trace`, then `full`.
- **Frida REPL needs a tty.** Backgrounded `frida` dies instantly if stdin is `/dev/null`; use a fifo (see [Frida](/docs/frida#background)).

## 4. Capture what the app sends [#4-capture-what-the-app-sends]

```bash
ls -t /tmp/mtflows/*.txt | head -5
cat "/tmp/mtflows/$(ls -t /tmp/mtflows | head -1)"
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open('/tmp/mtflows/_index.jsonl')]
for r in rows[-12:]:
    print(r['status'], r['method'], r['host']+r['path'][:70])
PY
```

Flows are `<HHMMSS>_<host>_<path>.txt` with request headers/body and response headers/body, plus a machine-readable `_index.jsonl`. Full format: [Flows](/docs/flows).

## 5. Replay with intent [#5-replay-with-intent]

```bash
session                                   # harvest cookies + localStorage from the WebView
replay --grep 'chat/loadInitialData' --session
replay --grep 'chat/loadInitialData' --session --patch 'conversationId="other-user"' --dry
replay --grep 'auth/session' --patch 'userName="victim@corp"' -x
```

`--dry` prints the exact request without sending — use it every time before a `--patch`. `-x` sends through mitmproxy so the attempt is captured as evidence.

## 6. Document as you go [#6-document-as-you-go]

```bash
recon com.example.app --deep      # static report first, before dynamic testing
```

Then write findings with the evidence pointer (`flow file`, `timestamp`, `endpoint`, `repro command`). A finding without a repro command is a rumour.

## Session hygiene [#session-hygiene]

- **One app at a time** on the emulator: `fdp` binds `:9222` and `fspawn` force-stops the package.
- Check `pentestctl status` after any reboot; `adb reverse` is always the first casualty.
- Long captures: `nettap status` prints flow count and the addon path, so you can tell "no traffic" from "addon not loaded".
- Credentials and tokens: keep them in `~/.mobsec/session/` (never in the repo, never in a screenshot).
